items.name: Vrat Cumin Sabudana Khichdi

ingredients.name: Potatoes, boiled and cut into cubes

steps: Drain the soaked pearls thoroughly and rub the coarse peanut meal through them so they separate.
Toast cumin in ghee, brown the potato cubes, and fold in the coated pearls over moderate heat.
Cover only until the centers turn translucent, then uncover, season, and add the lemon juice away from the flame.
items.guidance: Careful soaking keeps this fasting khichdi separate rather than gummy Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use fewer peanuts and potatoes and choose a small portion.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Baked Sabudana Vada
steps: Mix the drained pearls with the mashed potato, coarse peanuts, crushed cumin, chopped cilantro, and salt.
Shape compact patties with damp hands, arrange them on a warmed tray, and brush their surfaces lightly with melted ghee.
Bake until the bases are firm, turn each patty once, and continue until both faces are evenly golden.
items.guidance: Baking gives fasting sabudana patties a crisp surface with less fat Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: eat one small patty and increase cumin while reducing peanut.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Sabudana Potato Thalipeeth
steps: Knead the drained pearls, grated potato, fine peanut meal, cumin, and salt into a soft fasting dough.
Press one portion between damp palms, transfer it to a warm greased griddle, and thin it gently with wet fingertips.
Cook until the lower face releases, turn with a wide spatula, and brown the second side with only a trace more ghee.
items.guidance: A thin shape makes this sabudana thalipeeth crisper and easier to digest Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: keep the cake thin, use little ghee, and eat a modest serving.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Cardamom Sabudana Kheer
steps: Simmer the soaked pearls in part of the warmed milk until their centers become clear.
Pour in the remaining milk gradually and stir often as the kheer thickens around the translucent pearls.
Remove the pot from direct heat, dissolve the crushed rock sugar, and finish with cardamom and sliced pistachios.
items.guidance: This festival kheer is cooling and rich, so a small warm portion is sufficient Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: take only a few spoonfuls and reduce both sweetener and nuts.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Pumpkin Sabudana Pot

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into tiny cubes

steps: Soften cumin and grated ginger in ghee, then add the tiny pumpkin cubes and turn them until glossy.
Splash in hot water, cover until the pumpkin is nearly tender, and spread the drained pearls across the surface.
Cook gently until the pearls clear, folding only twice so the pumpkin remains visible, then season.
items.guidance: Pumpkin adds moisture to this fasting sabudana main Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce the pearl portion and add more ginger.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Sweet Potato Sabudana Pilaf

ingredients.name: Sweet potato, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Brown the sweet-potato cubes slowly in ghee with crushed fennel until their edges caramelize.
Add the drained pearls and chopped peanuts, cover briefly, and shake the pan as the centers turn translucent.
Uncover to release steam, season the pilaf, and sprinkle in the lemon juice once it leaves the heat.
items.guidance: Fennel balances the sweetness of this root-and-sabudana fasting pilaf Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chayote Sabudana Upma

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

steps: Toast cumin and ginger slivers in ghee, then sauté the chayote dice until their edges turn translucent.
Spread the drained pearls over the vegetable, cover for a few minutes, and lift them gently from below rather than stirring hard.
Stop cooking when the pearls are clear, season the upma, and scatter chopped cilantro over the loose mixture.
items.guidance: Juicy chayote keeps this fasting upma lighter than a potato version Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Lotus Seed Sabudana Khichdi

ingredients.name: Potatoes, boiled and cut into cubes

steps: Dry-roast the lotus seeds until crisp and break the larger ones into halves after they cool.
Bloom cumin and pepper in ghee, brown the potato cubes, and fold in the drained tapioca pearls.
Add the roasted seed halves when the pearls become translucent, toss gently, and season before serving warm.
items.guidance: Crisp lotus seeds contrast with soft pearls in this festival khichdi Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce both potato and ghee and keep the bowl small.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Coconut Lemon Sabudana
steps: Warm cumin in coconut oil and add the drained pearls in an even layer.
Cover briefly, then lift the pearls from the edges until they turn translucent without clumping.
Fold through the grated coconut and salt, remove the pan from heat, and finish with lemon juice and cilantro.
items.guidance: Coconut and lemon give sabudana a bright festival finish Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: use less lemon and eat the dish only warm, not hot. Kapha: keep coconut and oil light.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Soft Savory Sabudana Porridge
steps: Simmer the soaked pearls in hot water until they begin to lose their opaque centers.
Add the warmed almond drink, ground cumin, and grated ginger, then stir gently as the porridge becomes silky.
Season the soft mixture, draw it off the heat, and melt a little ghee across the surface before serving.
items.guidance: Extra liquid turns sabudana into a soft fasting breakfast rather than a dry pilaf Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Pumpkin Khichdi

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve
Pumpkin, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Warm cumin and grated ginger in ghee, then stir the tiny amaranth grains through the fragrant pot.
Add the pumpkin cubes and hot water, bring to a boil, and lower the heat under a partly covered lid.
Cook until the grains swell into a soft mass and the pumpkin yields, then season and rest the khichdi.
items.guidance: Pumpkin softens the earthy character of amaranth in this fasting khichdi Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Fennel Porridge

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve

steps: Simmer the rinsed amaranth in hot water until the grains swell and the liquid looks glossy.
Pour in the warmed oat drink, add ground fennel, and continue stirring until the porridge is creamy.
Take the pot off the flame before dissolving the crushed rock sugar and scattering in the cardamom.
items.guidance: Fennel makes this amaranth fasting porridge gently aromatic Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Potato Flatbread
steps: Combine the amaranth flour with mashed potato, crushed cumin, cilantro, and salt, adding hot water only as needed.
Pat a dough portion into a thin round between oiled sheets and peel away the upper sheet carefully.
Transfer the round to a warm griddle, cook until firm, and brown both faces with a light brushing of ghee.
items.guidance: Mashed potato makes gluten-free amaranth dough pliable enough for a fasting flatbread Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: make the breads thin and limit both potato and ghee.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Pumpkin Pancake
steps: Whisk the amaranth flour with mashed pumpkin, ground fennel, salt, and enough warm almond drink for a thick batter.
Rest the mixture briefly, then spoon small rounds onto a greased griddle and spread them without pressing.
Wait until the edges dry before turning each pancake, and cook the second face until the center feels set.
items.guidance: Pumpkin keeps these fasting amaranth pancakes tender without eggs Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Sesame Laddoo

ingredients.name: Sesame seeds, toasted and ground coarse

steps: Toast the popped amaranth and coarse sesame together until the mixture smells nutty.
Melt the grated jaggery with a spoonful of water, cook it to a sticky syrup, and stir in the warm ghee.
Work the hot syrup and cardamom through the grains, then shape small balls with lightly greased palms before the mixture cools.
items.guidance: These dense festival sweets combine popped amaranth with sesame and jaggery Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: eat only one small ball and reduce the sweetener.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Cardamom Kheer

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve

steps: Cook the rinsed amaranth in a portion of the warmed milk until the grains bloom and soften.
Add the remaining milk in stages, stirring the base so it thickens without catching on the pot.
Remove the kheer from direct heat, dissolve the crushed rock sugar, and finish with cardamom and sliced almonds.
items.guidance: Amaranth gives this fasting milk pudding a fine, bead-like texture Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: choose a small warm portion with less sweetener and fewer almonds.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Chayote Pot

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve
Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

steps: Bloom cumin and ginger slivers in ghee, then add the chayote dice and turn them until glossy.
Stir in the rinsed amaranth and hot water, bring the pot to a boil, and lower the heat.
Cook partly covered until the grains thicken around the tender vegetable, then season and rest before serving.
items.guidance: Chayote adds welcome moisture to a simple amaranth fasting meal Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Potato Pilaf

ingredients.name: Amaranth grain, rinsed in a fine sieve
Potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Brown the potato cubes in ghee with cumin until their edges develop a light crust.
Add the amaranth, cracked pepper, and hot water, then cover as soon as the pot returns to a boil.
Cook until the grains are tender and the liquid is absorbed, loosen the pilaf gently, and season.
items.guidance: Potato makes this amaranth pilaf particularly grounding Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: reduce the potato and ghee and increase black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Amaranth Sesame Brittle
steps: Combine the popped amaranth, toasted sesame, and ground cardamom in a warm bowl.
Melt the grated jaggery with a spoonful of water and cook until a drop firms quickly in cool water.
Stir in the grain mixture, spread it thinly on a greased tray, and score small pieces before the brittle hardens.
items.guidance: A thin sheet keeps this concentrated festival brittle appropriately portioned Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: limit the serving to one small piece.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Apple Amaranth Bake

ingredients.name: Apples, peeled and cut into wedges

steps: Arrange the apple wedges in a greased baking dish and dust them evenly with ground cinnamon.
Mix the popped amaranth with chopped almonds and melted ghee, then scatter the rough topping over the fruit.
Drizzle lightly with maple syrup and bake until the apples soften and the topping becomes crisp at the edges.
items.guidance: Baking makes fruit appropriate for a warm festival dessert without combining it with milk Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Cumin Khichdi

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Warm cumin and grated ginger in ghee, then brown the potato cubes lightly in the aromatic pot.
Stir in the buckwheat groats and hot water, cover, and cook gently until the grains split and soften.
Rest the khichdi off the heat, fluff it without crushing the potato, and season before serving.
items.guidance: Buckwheat makes this fasting khichdi warming and comparatively light Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Potato Roti
steps: Mix the buckwheat flour with mashed potato, crushed cumin, and salt, adding warm water until the dough holds.
Pat a small portion between greased sheets into an even round and peel back the upper sheet.
Lay the roti on a hot griddle, wait until it firms before turning, and brown both sides with a trace of ghee.
items.guidance: Potato binds fragile buckwheat flour for a practical fasting roti Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Fennel Dosa
steps: Whisk the buckwheat flour with yogurt, ground fennel, ginger, salt, and enough water for a flowing batter.
Rest the batter briefly, then pour a thin spiral onto a hot griddle and fill the gaps with the back of the ladle.
Drizzle a little ghee around the edge, turn when the surface dries, and cook the second side only until set.
items.guidance: Fennel and a short yogurt rest soften the earthy flavor of buckwheat dosa Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Pumpkin Chilla
steps: Whisk the buckwheat flour with mashed pumpkin, crushed cumin, cilantro, salt, and enough water for a thick batter.
Spoon a modest round onto a greased griddle and spread it gently so the pumpkin remains evenly distributed.
Turn after the lower face releases cleanly, then cook the second side until the center no longer feels damp.
items.guidance: Pumpkin keeps this fasting buckwheat chilla moist and naturally sweet Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Dumpling Kadhi
steps: Knead buckwheat flour and mashed potato with salt, then roll the soft dough into small fasting dumplings.
Poach the dumplings until they rise and firm, lift them out, and whisk the yogurt into the warm cooking liquid.
Simmer the kadhi gently with cumin bloomed in ghee, return the dumplings, and warm them until they absorb the tangy broth.
items.guidance: Poached buckwheat dumplings make this fasting kadhi satisfying without deep frying Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: serve fewer dumplings and use a thinner, well-spiced broth.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Sweet Potato Cakes
steps: Work the buckwheat flour, mashed sweet potato, crushed fennel, and salt into a soft, non-sticky mixture.
Shape small flat cakes, place them on a warm tray, and brush both exposed surfaces sparingly with melted ghee.
Bake until the bottoms set, turn each cake, and continue until the edges are dry and lightly browned.
items.guidance: Sweet potato binds these baked buckwheat fasting cakes Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: choose one small cake and keep the brushing very light.

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Pumpkin Stew

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into chunks
Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

steps: Toast cumin and ginger slivers in ghee, then stir the buckwheat groats until they smell nutty.
Pour in hot water and simmer until the grains begin to soften before adding the pumpkin chunks.
Cook the stew until the pumpkin thickens the broth naturally, season it, and rest the pot for five minutes.
items.guidance: A brothier preparation balances the dry, warming nature of buckwheat Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Almond Porridge
steps: Simmer the buckwheat groats in hot water until they split and become tender.
Add the warmed almond drink and continue cooking until the mixture reaches a loose porridge consistency.
Remove the pot from heat, stir in the crushed rock sugar and cardamom, and garnish with sliced almonds.
items.guidance: Plant milk keeps this sweet buckwheat fasting porridge gentle and dairy-free Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Jaggery Halwa
steps: Roast the buckwheat flour in ghee over low heat until its color deepens and the aroma turns nutty.
Pour in hot water gradually while stirring firmly, and cook until the paste leaves the sides of the pan.
Fold in the grated jaggery away from fierce heat, then finish the halwa with cardamom and broken cashews.
items.guidance: This concentrated fasting halwa is best treated as a small festival portion Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: limit the serving to two spoonfuls and reduce ghee and jaggery.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Buckwheat Chayote Pilaf

ingredients.name: Chayote, peeled and cut into small cubes

steps: Warm cumin and crushed fennel in ghee, then sauté the chayote cubes until their edges turn translucent.
Add the buckwheat groats and hot water, cover the pot, and cook gently until the grains are tender.
Let the pilaf stand off the heat, fluff it carefully so the chayote remains intact, and season.
items.guidance: Moist chayote moderates buckwheat in this simple fasting pilaf Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chestnut Potato Flatbread
steps: Combine the chestnut meal with mashed potato, crushed cumin, and salt to form a soft fasting dough.
Press a portion between greased sheets into a small even round and lift away the upper sheet.
Cook the flatbread on a warm griddle until firm enough to turn, then brown the second face with a little ghee.
items.guidance: Chestnut and potato create a naturally sweet singhara-style fasting bread Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chestnut Fennel Crepes
steps: Whisk the chestnut meal with ground fennel, salt, warm almond drink, and enough water for a thin batter.
Pour a small ladleful onto a greased griddle and tilt the pan so the batter forms a delicate round.
Loosen the edge once dry, turn the crepe carefully, and cook the second face for less than a minute.
items.guidance: Thin cooking keeps these sweet chestnut fasting crepes light Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chestnut Pumpkin Dumplings
steps: Mix the chestnut meal with mashed pumpkin, crushed cumin, and salt until the soft dough holds a shape.
Roll small dumplings with damp hands, arrange them in a steamer, and cook until their surfaces become firm.
Transfer them to a warm tray, brush with melted ghee, and bake briefly to dry the outer layer.
items.guidance: Steaming before baking gives these fasting dumplings a tender center Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chestnut Potato Cakes
steps: Toss the grated potato with chestnut meal, cracked pepper, chopped cilantro, and salt without overworking it.
Compress the mixture into small cakes and brush their tops with a thin sheen of melted ghee.
Bake until the bases brown, turn each cake once, and continue until the edges become crisp.
items.guidance: Chestnut meal helps these fasting potato cakes hold together without eggs Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: eat one small cake and use little ghee.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chestnut Cardamom Halwa
steps: Roast the chestnut meal in ghee until the mixture becomes fragrant and slightly darker.
Add hot water in a steady stream while stirring, then cook until the paste becomes glossy and thick.
Draw the pan from high heat, dissolve the crushed rock sugar, and finish with ground cardamom.
items.guidance: Chestnut makes a naturally sweet fasting halwa that needs only modest added sugar Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: serve two small spoonfuls and reduce the ghee.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chestnut Oat-Milk Porridge
steps: Whisk the chestnut meal into hot water in a thin stream so it disperses without lumps.
Add the warmed oat drink and ground fennel, then simmer while stirring until the porridge coats the spoon.
Take the pot off the flame, dissolve the crushed rock sugar, and serve the porridge warm.
items.guidance: Plant milk keeps this singhara-style fasting porridge free of fruit-dairy concerns Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chestnut Pumpkin Pancakes
steps: Whisk the chestnut meal, mashed pumpkin, cinnamon, salt, and warm almond drink into a thick batter.
Drop small rounds onto a lightly greased griddle and let their edges dry before moving them.
Turn each pancake with a broad spatula and cook until the second side browns and the center sets.
items.guidance: Pumpkin and chestnut produce tender egg-free fasting pancakes Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chestnut Sweet Potato Roti
steps: Knead the chestnut meal with mashed sweet potato, crushed fennel, and salt until the mixture forms a pliable dough.
Pat each portion between greased sheets into a thin round, repairing any cracks with damp fingertips.
Cook the roti on a hot griddle, turn only after the first side firms, and finish with a sparse brushing of ghee.
items.guidance: Sweet potato binds chestnut meal in this soft fasting roti Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Steamed Chestnut Cakes
steps: Beat the chestnut meal with yogurt, crushed cumin, ginger, salt, and enough water for a thick spoonable batter.
Rest the mixture while greasing shallow cups, then divide it evenly without packing it down.
Steam until the centers feel firm, let the cakes settle briefly, and release them while still warm.
items.guidance: Steam keeps these singhara-style fasting cakes moist without frying Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Chestnut Milk Pudding
steps: Whisk the chestnut meal into a small portion of warmed milk until perfectly smooth.
Pour the slurry into the remaining milk and simmer slowly, stirring the base as it thickens.
Remove the pudding from direct heat, dissolve the crushed rock sugar, and garnish with cardamom and pistachios.
items.guidance: Chestnut thickens this fruit-free festival milk pudding naturally Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: take a small portion and use less sweetener.

items.name: Vrat Fennel Lotus Seed Curry
steps: Dry-roast the lotus seeds until crisp, cool them, and crack the largest pieces in half.
Soften the diced fennel bulb in ghee, add ground fennel and hot water, and simmer until the broth is fragrant.
Lower the heat before folding in the yogurt and roasted seeds, then warm gently without letting the curry boil.
items.guidance: Fennel keeps this fasting lotus-seed yogurt curry mild Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use less yogurt and ghee and choose a small bowl.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Pepper Roasted Lotus Seeds
steps: Warm the dry-roasted lotus seeds in a broad pan until their centers become crisp.
Drizzle over the melted ghee and toss continuously so every seed receives only a light coating.
Sprinkle in cracked pepper, ground cumin, and salt, then cool the snack in a single layer.
items.guidance: A light ghee coating carries pepper and cumin across these crisp fasting seeds Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Lotus Seed Saffron Kheer
steps: Crush the roasted lotus seeds into a mixture of coarse crumbs and small pieces.
Simmer them in the warmed milk until the crumbs thicken the liquid and the larger pieces soften.
Remove the kheer from fierce heat, dissolve the crushed rock sugar, and add the soaked saffron and cardamom.
items.guidance: Lotus-seed crumbs give this festival kheer body without grain Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: serve a small warm portion with less sweetener.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Cumin Potato Curry

ingredients.name: Potatoes, boiled and broken into chunks
Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

steps: Toast cumin and ginger slivers in ghee, then reduce the chopped tomatoes until their raw scent fades.
Add the broken potato chunks and hot water, crush a few pieces into the broth, and simmer until thick.
Season the fasting curry and scatter chopped cilantro over it after turning off the flame.
items.guidance: Broken potatoes naturally thicken this simple cumin fasting curry Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: replace part of the tomato with pumpkin and reduce ginger. Kapha: choose a small serving and reduce ghee.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Pumpkin Coconut Stew

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into chunks
Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

steps: Simmer the pumpkin chunks with ginger slivers until they are tender but still hold their corners.
Grind the coconut with cumin and hot broth, then fold the smooth paste through the pot.
Season the stew, remove it from direct heat, and finish the surface with a restrained drizzle of coconut oil.
items.guidance: A mild coconut broth makes pumpkin suitable for a quiet fasting main Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Baked Yam Patties
steps: Mix the mashed yam with chestnut meal, crushed cumin, chopped cilantro, and salt.
Shape broad thin patties, arrange them on a warmed tray, and brush the tops sparingly with melted ghee.
Bake until the lower surfaces brown, turn each patty, and continue until the edges feel firm.
items.guidance: Chestnut meal gives these festival yam patties structure without grain Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: eat one thin patty and use little ghee.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Baked Green Plantain Cutlets
steps: Work the mashed plantain with crushed popped amaranth, cumin, pepper, and salt until evenly combined.
Form small oval cutlets, place them on a greased tray, and brush their exposed sides lightly with ghee.
Bake until set, turn the cutlets carefully, and finish when both surfaces are dry and golden.
items.guidance: Popped amaranth gives baked plantain cutlets a delicate crust Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: limit the portion and keep the ghee light.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Warm Papaya Pomegranate Plate

ingredients.name: Papaya, peeled and cut into thick slices

steps: Warm the papaya slices briefly in a covered pan until their chill is gone but their shape remains firm.
Arrange the softened fruit on plates and scatter the pomegranate arils over the surface.
Finish with crushed fennel, sliced mint, and a light squeeze of lime immediately before serving.
items.guidance: Serving fruit without dairy keeps this fasting plate simple and traditionally compatible Vata: warm the papaya thoroughly and use little lime. Pitta: omit the lime if the fruit is already tart. Kapha: keep the portion moderate.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Almond Date Laddoo
steps: Warm the chopped dates in a dry pan until they soften into a sticky mass.
Fold in the coarse almonds, shredded coconut, cardamom, and warmed coconut oil until evenly distributed.
Cool the mixture just enough to handle, then roll small festival balls and let them firm uncovered.
items.guidance: Dates bind these dairy-free fasting sweets without added sugar Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: eat only one small ball.
provenance: original lacto-vegetarian recipe developed for the R3 regional and practical cooking collection

items.name: Vrat Taro Lotus Seed Pot

ingredients.name: Taro root, peeled and cut into chunks
Fresh ginger, cut into fine slivers

steps: Parboil the taro chunks until their surfaces soften, drain them carefully, and leave them intact.
Toast cumin and ginger slivers in ghee, add the taro, and turn the pieces until their edges take on color.
Pour in hot water and the roasted lotus-seed halves, simmer until the broth thickens, and season the fasting pot.
items.guidance: Ginger and crisp lotus seeds balance the grounding weight of taro Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: choose a small portion and use less ghee.
